setup_summary.text: The 3Q26 print came out on 2026-10-30, so the next report is 4Q26 on 2027-01-28 (88 days out). 3Q26 GAAP earnings were $15.4B ($3.72/share) and adjusted earnings were $17.5B ($4.23/share). That compares with 2Q26 GAAP of $14.5B ($3.48) and adjusted of $14.7B ($3.52).

3Q26 operating cash flow was $25.7B and free cash flow was $19.1B. Shareholder distributions were $9.4B ($4.3B dividends, $5.1B buybacks). Net debt was $22.1B (debt $34.3B less cash $12.2B), and management cites roughly $11B of year-to-date net debt reduction.

Consensus for 4Q26 is EPS of $3.95 and revenue of $113.77B. That sits between 3Q26 GAAP EPS ($3.72) and adjusted EPS ($4.23), about 6% below adjusted and 6% above GAAP. Whether consensus is on a GAAP or adjusted basis is not stated, so the gap in the print could be large either way. Revenue consensus is close to 3Q26 total revenues and other income of $113.2B (sales and other operating revenue was $110.5B).

Caution on the derived growth rates (F.57, F.59). They compare 4Q26 consensus with 3Q25 ($85.29B revenue, $1.76 EPS), which is the wrong base. Backing out 9M25 from FY25 gives 4Q25 total revenues and other income of about $82.3B and EPS of about $1.54, with net income of about $6.5B. Against that base, consensus implies roughly +38% revenue and +156% EPS year on year. The comparison is easy because 4Q25 was weak.

Earnings were driven by the market backdrop in 3Q26: Brent averaged $97.01/b (2Q26: $104.52), the indicative refining margin was $50.3/b (2Q26: $29.0), and TTF was $18.20. Management says the Middle East conflict cost it roughly 10% of upstream production in 2Q, and industry refining capacity was constrained.

The stock trades at $187.25 against a consensus price target of $171.11 (-8.6%). Over the last 8 reports the average closing move was ±1.1%. The company beat in 3 of the last 4 quarters, with an average surprise of +3.9%. Barclays and Morgan Stanley both maintained Overweight in October.

Structural cost savings reached $16.9B cumulative vs 2019, including $1.8B in the first nine months of 2026. The target is $20B by 2030. Management says 2026 cash opex ex energy and production taxes is running roughly flat year on year.

since_filing.text: Since the 10-Q (2026-08-03), the company has reported 3Q26: GAAP earnings of $15.4B and adjusted earnings of $17.5B. The 8-K figures are consistent with the 10-Q on a year-to-date basis (H1 operating cash flow $32.26B plus 3Q $25.65B equals the YTD $57.9B), so there are no contradictions to flag.

Segment mix changed sharply between 2Q and 3Q (adjusted earnings). Energy Products rose to $9,053M from $4,099M. Upstream fell to $7,308M from $9,189M, on lower prices and an accelerated Guyana entitlement impact. Chemical Products fell to $725M from $1,214M, and Specialty Products rose to $1,283M from $969M.

The company announced $20B of 2027 buybacks and a 4Q dividend raise to $1.07. It noted record year-to-date refining operating performance (highest diesel yield and North American diesel volumes) and accumulated Upstream milestones in Guyana, Kearl and PNG LNG.
The balance sheet strengthened. Net debt was $22.1B at 30 September, versus about $31.8B at 30 June (derived: $42.4B debt less $10.6B cash) and $32.9B at year-end. Total debt was $34.3B.
The redomicile to Texas completed on 1 July. The 3Q balance sheet shows equity reshuffled (par stock and capital in excess of par; treasury shares largely cancelled), with no effect on total equity.
The Louisiana coastal litigation was settled effective 31 July. The 10-Q says 2Q reserves captured the estimated impact and 3Q impact was expected to be immaterial.
The CEO told CNBC on 2026-10-30 that the company is producing record volumes of diesel in North America. This is a headline-level corroboration of the 8-K, with no new financial data.

Sell-side and valuation context is lean. Barclays (10-19) and Morgan Stanley (10-15) maintained Overweight. The consensus price target of $171.11 is below the $187.25 share price. The only other news in the last 14 days is a generic Seeking Alpha piece, which is not citable for specifics.

key_debates.question: Is 3Q's earnings power sustainable into 4Q, or did margins peak in 3Q?

bull.text: Consensus EPS of $3.95 sits below 3Q adjusted EPS of $4.23, so the bar is lower than the last quarter's run rate. Refining margins went to $50.3/b in 3Q from $29.0/b, and the CEO expects very high margins to persist while about 3 million b/d of capacity remains offline. Structural savings and advantaged volumes add earnings power that does not depend on price.

bear.text: Brent has fallen from $104.52 in 2Q to $97.01 in 3Q. Upstream adjusted earnings fell $1.9B quarter on quarter, and Chemical Products fell 40% on weaker margins. The spike in margins is linked to supply disruptions that could reverse. The stock is above the consensus price target.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The 4Q realised refining margin and Brent averages against 3Q, and adjusted EPS compared with $3.95 once the basis of consensus is known.

key_debates.question: How much of the GAAP-to-adjusted gap is transitory (timing effects) versus recurring (identified items)?

bull.text: 3Q estimated timing effects were -$2.5B, with -$3.9B YTD. These effects unwind in later periods, so they set up a possible GAAP tailwind. 3Q identified items were net positive at +$0.4B on a $675M gain on sale of assets.

bear.text: YTD identified items are -$2.9B, including $1.57B of reserve additions and $921M of Middle East impacts (hedge-related shipments that could not physically settle). Impairments of $1.1B also hit 2Q. A recurring pattern of one-time charges undermines the adjusted view, and reserve additions may continue.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The 4Q reconciliation table of identified items and timing effects, and whether Middle East hedge impacts and reserve additions repeat.

key_debates.question: Is the Guyana entitlement change a value-neutral inflection or a volume headwind?

bull.text: Management says the project recovered its $55B investment about two years early, so the production-sharing terms move to 50-50 profit share after the 75% cost-recovery cap. This is an inflection in free cash flow with 2x the 2025 level expected by 2030, plus more upside from Longtail, a possible ninth FPSO and AI-identified prospects.

bear.text: Net entitlement volumes fall as cost-recovery barrels shrink (-87 koebd of price/spend entitlements in 3Q), and management said the effect came earlier than expected. Reported production is already flat to down (4,496 koebd vs 4,514 in 2Q, and below the prior year in 2Q), so volume growth leans on the Permian and new FPSOs.

key_debates.what_settles_it: 4Q koebd and the volume bridge, any disclosed 2027 production outlook, and the start-up timing of Errea Wittu.

key_debates.question: Will chemicals recover from the 3Q margin retreat?

bull.text: North American ethane feed advantage persists (USGC ethane $180/T), reliability is at record levels, and Asia supply constraints supported the 2Q margin spike. High-value product volumes grew in 3Q on seasonal Asia Pacific demand.

bear.text: Chemical Products earnings fell from $1,131M to $735M quarter on quarter, and North American polyethylene fell about 31% to $998/T. Chemical margins were below the bottom of the 10-year range, and 2025 showed how fast oversupply can compress earnings.

key_debates.what_settles_it: 4Q polyethylene and ethylene margin markers, Chemical Products earnings, and management's comment on Asia.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: 4Q26 EPS beats $3.95 on a basis comparable to consensus. Refining margins stay well above $29/b and diesel supply remains tight, timing effects reverse into GAAP earnings, and Errea Wittu starts early. Free cash flow and buybacks stay strong, and 2027 plans reinforce the $20B buyback. The stock's average move is small (±1.1%), so a beat has limited impact unless there is an upside surprise to 2027 guidance.

triggers: 4Q refining margin average at or above the 3Q level of $50.3/b
Large positive reversal of estimated timing effects
Upstream production back above 4.5 Moebd as Middle East volumes return

scenarios.name: base

description.text: 4Q26 EPS lands close to $3.95. Lower Brent trims Upstream earnings, which strong refining margins and about 1.5–2% share-count shrinkage partly offset. Timing effects are neutral to slightly positive for GAAP, and identified items are modest. Capex of about $7–8B and buybacks of about $5B give free cash flow near $17–19B.

triggers: Refining margins retreat from the 3Q peak but stay above 2Q levels
No major new reserves or impairments

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: 4Q26 EPS misses $3.95. Oil and refining margins ease as disruption fades or demand slows, Chemicals fall further, and additional identified items appear (financial reserves, impairments, Middle East supply impacts). A European windfall tax on refining adds an extra charge. Working capital reverses 3Q's inflow, free cash flow falls short, and the stock, already above the average target, pulls back.

triggers: Brent and refining margins fall sharply versus 3Q
Strait of Hormuz reopens faster, compressing margins and refining spreads
New Middle East hedge or shipping impacts, reserve additions or impairments
European windfall taxes enacted on downstream earnings
Production slips below 4.4 Moebd on outages or entitlements

claim.text: Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption. About 10% of upstream production was lost in 2Q, Qatar LNG trains need repair with Qatar Energy still in talks, and volatility in shipping and attacks inhibits transit. The same disruption supports margins, so a resolution is both a volume tailwind and a margin headwind.

Commodity price and margin mean reversion. Brent has already fallen 7% sequentially, and the refining margin of $50.3/b is far above levels seen over the last year ($18.3/b in 4Q25). The 10-K notes that a material price increase can hurt downstream results and a decline hurts upstream results.

Windfall and punitive taxes on refining. One European country has approved a windfall tax on the downstream, and the CEO said the company canceled investments after the previous windfall tax. ExxonMobil has about 850 kbd of refining in the UK and Europe.

Earnings quality: unfavorable estimated timing effects (-$3.9B YTD) and recurring identified items (-$2.9B YTD, including $1.57B of financial reserve additions) make GAAP earnings volatile relative to adjusted earnings. The 10-Q flags that variable trading and derivative impacts affect results each quarter.
Tax-rate volatility. The effective rate has ranged from 40% in 1Q to 24% in 2Q and 26% in 3Q on jurisdiction mix, so small shifts can move quarterly EPS.

Project execution and volume risk. This includes Guyana entitlement reductions after cost recovery, the timing of FPSO start-ups, Golden Pass LNG ramp-up, and the Kazakhstan/CPC export route, which supplied about 320 kboe/d and $1.1B of 2025 earnings and could be disrupted.

Working-capital and liquidity swings. Receivables rose to $66.5B and payables to $78.6B. Operating cash flow was helped by a 3Q inflow, so a reversal would cut 4Q cash flow. Net debt is low, so balance sheet risk is limited.

Valuation and expectations risk. The share price is 9% above the consensus price target, and a large run in energy stocks has raised expectations. Analysts are not publicly negative, but the margin for error on the print may be thinner than the ±1.1% average post-earnings move suggests.

questions_for_management.question: What are the 4Q expectations for estimated timing effects and identified items, and do you expect further Middle East hedge-shipment impacts after the $921M year to date?

why.text: The 3Q GAAP-to-adjusted gap was about $2.1B, and YTD timing effects are -$3.9B. These drive the gap versus a consensus of unknown basis.

questions_for_management.question: How much Upstream volume is still offline in the Middle East, and what is the status and timeline of the Qatar LNG train repairs and your role in them?

why.text: Middle East disruptions cost about 10% of upstream production in 2Q, and 3Q volumes of 4,496 koebd did not recover. Management says it is discussing repairs with Qatar Energy.

questions_for_management.question: What is the size of the Guyana entitlement change in 4Q and 2027, and what does the 2030 plan imply for net volumes and free cash flow?

why.text: Entitlements cost 87 koebd in 3Q, management said the effect came earlier than planned, and the plan will be updated with the corporate plan at year-end.

questions_for_management.question: What are 4Q margin capture and turnaround plans for Energy Products, and how sustainable is the record distillate yield if Middle East supply returns?

why.text: Energy Products adjusted earnings more than doubled to $9.05B on a $50.3/b margin. Planned maintenance was a headwind in 2Q, and management has deferred some turnarounds.

questions_for_management.question: What is the 2027 capex framework relative to the $27–29B 2026 range, and what is the 4Q cash capex run rate?

why.text: The range implies $7–9B for 4Q. The company has announced $20B of 2027 buybacks, so the capex plan determines the free cash flow coverage of dividends and buybacks.

questions_for_management.question: Which items drove the $1.57B of financial reserve additions this year, and is there more exposure?

why.text: Reserve additions of $1.2B hit Upstream in 2Q, and a Louisiana settlement was reached. They are a recurring cause of GAAP shortfalls versus adjusted earnings.

questions_for_management.question: What is the outlook for the effective tax rate and Corporate and Financing costs in 4Q and 2027?

why.text: The tax rate was 40%, 24% and 26% in three consecutive quarters, and Corporate and Financing costs have run about $0.9B per quarter.

questions_for_management.question: How does management view the Errea Wittu start-up date and the Rovuma and Papua FID timing, now that working interests are rising?

why.text: The FPSO is guided for year-end, and FIDs are guided for later this year. The 8-K says working interests in Papua and Rovuma are increasing to 34% and 50%, which affects capex and cash flow.
